knowledgePattern: Derive a recurrence for reciprocal power sums

hints.title: Find the simplest reciprocal relation
hints.body: Use the given quadratic to relate x and its reciprocal, first checking that division by x is allowed.
hints.recap: Cancellation or division is valid only when the divisor is nonzero.
hints.pitfall: The zeroth power also appears in the sequence definition.
hints.pause: Calculate the first two sequence values.

recall.reminder: Cancellation or division is valid only when the divisor is nonzero.

hints.title: Expand a product of neighbouring powers
hints.body: Multiply the simple reciprocal relation by xn−1+x−(n−1), then group the resulting terms using the sequence definition.
hints.recap: Multiplication by x increases an exponent by one; multiplication by its reciprocal decreases it by one.
hints.pitfall: A two-term recurrence needs both starting values and the correct index.
hints.pause: Derive the recurrence coefficient and calculate the requested term.

recall.reminder: Multiplication by x increases an exponent by one; multiplication by its reciprocal decreases it by one.

solution:
1. The quadratic has nonzero constant term, so x≠0. Dividing by x gives x+1/x=3. The initial values are p0=2 and p1=3.

2. For n≥2, expand (x+1/x)(xn−1+x−(n−1)). Its outer terms give pn and its middle terms give pn−2. Thus 3pn−1=pn+pn−2, or pn=3pn−1−pn−2.

3. The successive values are p2=7, p3=18, p4=47, p5=123 and p6=322. Answer A.
